title: Virtual Interface Binding
description: Explain why class-based testbenches use virtual interfaces and how they are connected to concrete interface instances.
task: Describe declaration, assignment and use of a virtual interface handle in a driver or monitor.
constraints: Distinguish interface instances from virtual interface handles.

title: throughout Operator
description: Use the SVA throughout operator to require a condition for the full duration of another sequence.
task: Explain how throughout differs from repeating a single-cycle implication and give a handshake-related example.
starterCode: // Explain and apply the throughout operator.

title: UVM Phase Objections
description: Explain how UVM objections control the lifetime of time-consuming phases.
task: Describe where raise_objection and drop_objection belong in a test and what can go wrong when they are misused.
examples: raise before starting stimulus; drop after stimulus and drain time
constraints: Do not raise permanent objections in low-level components.
starterCode: // Explain correct objection usage in run_phase.

title: AXI-Lite Write Channel Ordering
description: Reason about the independent AXI-Lite write-address and write-data channels.
task: Explain why AWVALID and WVALID may arrive in different cycles and how a slave can safely accept and pair them before issuing BVALID.
examples: Address and data handshakes are independent
constraints: Do not assume AW and W handshake simultaneously.
Explain when the write response becomes legal.
